framework.summary: The Secretary must consider basing the required shutdown capability on a graduated deployment-corrections framework (throttle, restrict, suspend, shut down); developers write no safety framework.
framework.quote: Requiring a technical capability based on a graduated deployment-corrections framework that applies when there is evidence of a credible risk of a covered incident

transparency_report.summary: The bill requires no public report or disclosure about a model.

incident_reporting.summary: The Secretary must by rule require covered entities to report a covered incident (shutdown sabotage, major deaths or damage, concealment, loss of control) within 15 days of becoming aware.
incident_reporting.quote: Not later than 15 days after such covered entity becomes aware of a covered incident relating to such technology, submit to the Secretary a report regarding such incident.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no shorter reporting window for imminent risk.

third_party_audit.summary: After a shutdown order, the Secretary (a government body, not an independent auditor) must audit or inspect to verify compliance; developers need no independent audit.
third_party_audit.quote: shall through audit, telemetry, on-site inspection, or other forensic review verify compliance with the order that prompted such confirmation.

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no whistleblower protections.

registration.summary: The bill sets no registration or licensing requirement.

shutdown.summary: The Secretary must by rule require covered entities to keep the technical ability to stop inference, end or suspend user access, and shut down the technology.

compute_threshold.summary: Covered technology is AI built with computing power that would cost more than $100,000,000 at market cloud prices, as the Secretary determines.
compute_threshold.quote: developed utilizing a quantity of computing power the cost of which would exceed $100,000,000 at the prevailing market price of cloud computing in the United States

revenue_threshold.summary: A covered entity must earn at least $500,000,000 in gross revenue from the technology, with affiliates, in the prior calendar year.
revenue_threshold.quote: Derives together with the affiliates, if any, of such person not less than $500,000,000 in gross revenue from such technology in the calendar year preceding the calendar year at issue.

harm_threshold.summary: A covered incident includes unintended AI conduct causing at least 10 deaths or at least $100,000,000 in economic damages, plus shutdown sabotage, concealment and loss of control.
harm_threshold.quote: causes the death of not fewer than 10 individuals or economic damages of not less than $100,000,000

penalties.summary: The Secretary may assess civil penalties up to $2,000,000 per day, or up to $20,000,000 per day for violating a shutdown order; the Attorney General can also sue.
penalties.quote: the Secretary may assess on such covered entity a civil penalty of not more than $2,000,000 for each day on which such violation occurs.

effective_date.summary: The bill states no effective date; it sets rulemaking deadlines of 90 days after enactment.

notes: Amends the Homeland Security Act; requirements take effect through Secretary rulemaking (90 days after enactment), so effective_date marked not_in_bill. Covered entity/technology definitions are updated annually by rule.
